name: Combined oral contraceptive pill for acne

card.summary: Estrogen-plus-progestin birth control pills that the FDA has cleared for moderate acne in women who also want contraception; effective for many, with clotting risk attached.
card.aka: The pill for acne; COC; Yaz, Ortho Tri-Cyclen, Estrostep, Beyaz
card.note: Prescription-only; raises venous clotting risk, with differences by progestin.

quick.overview:
Combined oral contraceptive pills contain an estrogen and a progestin. Because they lower androgen activity, some formulations are used to treat acne in women, and the US FDA has approved four of them for moderate acne in patients who also need contraception.

It is a hormonal option discussed in dermatology rather than a looksmaxxing-specific protocol, and is relevant only to people who can use these pills.
quick.mechanism: The estrogen component suppresses ovarian androgen production and raises sex hormone-binding globulin, which lowers free testosterone. Lower androgens reduce sebum production, a driver of acne [1].
quick.risks: Common effects include breakthrough bleeding, nausea, headache and breast tenderness. Venous thromboembolism risk is raised in users and varies by progestin, and arterial events are increased in smokers over 35 and people with migraine with aura. The FDA added a label warning for drospirenone-containing pills in 2012 [1].

lead: Combined oral contraceptive pills combine an estrogen with a progestin and are taken mainly to prevent pregnancy. Dermatologists also use them to treat acne in women because the hormonal changes they cause reduce sebum production [1].

Wikipedia reports that studies show combined pills reduce both inflammatory and non-inflammatory facial acne lesions, that head-to-head comparisons between brands have not been studied, and that progestin-only pills have not been shown to help acne [1]. The US FDA has approved four combined pills for moderate acne in patients aged at least 14 or 15 who have started menstruating and need contraception: Ortho Tri-Cyclen, Estrostep, Beyaz and YAZ [1].

paras: The FDA-approved acne indication applies to moderate acne in patients who have started menstruating and who also seek oral contraception [1]. Apart from acne, the FDA has approved no oral contraceptives for other conditions the pill is commonly used to treat [1].

Wikipedia summarises studies as showing reduced inflammatory and non-inflammatory facial lesions with combined pills, but notes no direct brand comparisons [1]. Detailed trial results are not given here. Registered trials returned for this topic concern contraception safety surveillance of YAZ in China (1,921 participants) rather than acne outcomes [2].
The most common side effect is breakthrough bleeding, followed by nausea, headache, bloating, breast tenderness and weight or fluid changes, which often fade with time [1].

Wikipedia reports venous thromboembolism risk of roughly 60 per 100,000 woman-years in users versus 30 in non-users, varying by progestin, with higher rate ratios than levonorgestrel for desogestrel, gestodene, drospirenone and cyproterone acetate [1]. An FDA review of drospirenone pills led to a 2012 label warning [1]. Ischemic stroke and heart attack risk is increased, especially with high estrogen doses, smoking over 35 or migraine with aura [1]. Contraindications include pregnancy, hypertension, prior thrombosis and liver tumours [1].

Progestogen feedback reduces GnRH pulses, lowering FSH and LH and preventing ovulation. For acne, estrogen lowers ovarian androgen production, raises SHBG and decreases free testosterone, and sebaceous glands shrink [1].
Oral contraceptives were first approved by the FDA for contraception in 1960 [1]. Later generations lowered estrogen dose and varied the progestin [1].

timeline.event: First oral contraceptive approved by the FDA [1].
FDA adds a label warning on VTE risk for drospirenone-containing pills [1].
